summary: Filippo De Filippi (1869–1938) worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at the University of Genoa and the University of Bologna.

Filippo Marsili works in sinology, history, and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, and Arcangela Santoro, and holds a post at Saint Louis University.

Finnian M. M. Gerety is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University in 2015 under Michael Witzel and Masato Fujii, completed a fellowship at Yale (2017–2018), and taught at Brown University (attested 2020).

Fitzedward Hall (1825–1901) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1850), Sanskrit College (1853), King's College London (1862), and the India Office (~1862–1869).

Flavio A. Geisshuesler works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Bern, Lausanne under Tom Tillemans and Pascale Hugon, and Virginia (~2014–2019, PhD) under David F. Germano, before holding a postdoctoral post at Hebrew University in 2019.
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she later taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bucharest, Waseda, and Hamburg (PhD under Lambert Schmithausen), holding posts at Kansai Medical University (1994–2001), ICPBS (2001), IIBS (~2008), and IRIAB (2009).

Florinda De Simini (born 1983) is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Turin (~2009–2013). She held posts at IIAS (2013), the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2015), and the University of Hamburg (~2016).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1971) and under Chögyam Trungpa (~1971–1975).

Francesco Sferra (born 1965) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Raffaele Torella (~1990–1999). He has held professorial and directorial posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~2002, ~2017) and Federico II (attested 2010–2016).
Francis Brinkley (1841–1912) was a specialist in Japanology. He studied at the Royal School Dungannon and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1881).

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton (1762–1829) studied at the University of Edinburgh (MD 1783). Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served in the Bengal Medical Service (~1794–1815) and directed the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden (1814–1815).

Francis Gladwin (1745–1812) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1812) and served as professor of Persian at Fort William College (~1801–1805).

Francis Harold Cook (born 1930) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1970). He was a professor at the University of California, Riverside (~1970–1989), becoming emeritus in ~1989.

Francis N. J. is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed a Master's degree in Ancient History and doctoral research under M. R. Raghava Varier at the University of Calicut (attested 2002).

Francis Vincent Tiso (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Cornell, Harvard, Columbia, and Union Theological Seminary, he teaches Tibetan Buddhism at the Pontifical Gregorian University.
Francis Wilford (1761–1822) was an Indologist and historian. He was a fellow member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1822) and served as secretary to the committee at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Francis Woodman Cleaves (1911–1995) worked in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth and Harvard (PhD ~1942), studied under Paul Pelliot (1935), and served as a professor at Harvard University (1941–1980).

Francis X. Clooney (born 1950) is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. After doctoral studies at the University of Chicago (~1978–1984), he was a professor at Boston College (1984–2005) and was appointed Parkman Professor at Harvard in 2005.
Francisco García Ayuso (1845–1897) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Munich under Martin Haug between ~1869 and 1872.
